title: After-hours jam sessions in Harlem
summary: He paints a picture of after-hours places where musicians jammed until morning.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: A little bit earlier, you were giving us a little idea, and I said I'd like to come back to it, of what the Harlem musical scene was like. And, you had even mentioned the Depression, and what kind of an overall feeling that was sort of going on then. Could you sort of tie that through?
You're talking about in Harlem in the 20s years?
Well, we was at the Ubanqi Club, I believe I said.
And, well, during that time, like the people from downtown, I always said from downtown because they closed up first, and Harlem always went until, until everybody got tired, I should say.
Now, what you want me to get in to is what the fun they had?
picture for us of what was going on so that we can feel it.

They had a place like, even like Billy Daniels used to go to Monroe's Place, after hours places, where they'd go down and have, where they'd have their after hours drink. They had a band down there in one of the clubs what they called a tramp band. Redd Foxx used to play along the strings of a bass. And then, we used to take our horns down there and have a little jam session. People would send us drinks. We would play there until 10:00 in the morning. We had musicians from different other bands used to come out. Roy Eldridge and myself have met up a few times there. Les Paul used to come up a lot with his guitar. He arrived from in the Savoy. We used to, after the last hour, they used to sit in and play. Then, they go from there. We used to go around looking for other after hour spots where we could jam and have fun. And, a lot of the public, they'd come up and find out where we were, and they'd follow us there.
